lessons.title: Campaign Warfare Overview — Tổng quan chiến dịch
lessons.objective: Hiểu campaign framework, types, và when to use each
lessons.content:
Campaign warfare = concentrated effort nhắm vào specific goal trong timeframe ngắn. Khác với routine operations, campaigns có START, PEAK, và END.

WHY CAMPAIGNS MATTER:

Routine operations: Consistent but slow growth
Campaigns: Explosive but requires preparation

Best leaders combine BOTH:
- 70% routine (maintain baseline)
- 30% campaigns (accelerate growth)

4 CAMPAIGN TYPES:

1. FLASH RECRUITMENT (72 giờ)
- Goal: 5+ new members
- When: Need quick team expansion, event-driven
- Structure: Day 1 awareness → Day 2 interest → Day 3 conversion
- Risk: Lower quality recruits if rushed
- Best practice: Pre-screen prospects before campaign

2. FLASH SALES (48 giờ)
- Goal: 10+ orders
- When: Need quick revenue, product launch, clearing inventory
- Structure: Announce → Urgency → Close
- Risk: Train customers to only buy on sale
- Best practice: Mix flash sales with regular pricing

3. AWARENESS CAMPAIGN (7 ngày)
- Goal: Reach 500+ new people
- When: Building brand, entering new segment
- Structure: Content series + engagement
- Risk: Low conversion from awareness alone
- Best practice: Always have follow-up system for new contacts

4. RETENTION CAMPAIGN (14 ngày)
- Goal: Re-engage 50%+ inactive members
- When: Member engagement dropping, quarterly review
- Structure: Personal outreach + value + invitation back
- Risk: Some members may have truly moved on
- Best practice: Personalize, don't blast

CAMPAIGN ANATOMY:

Every campaign has:

1. OBJECTIVE (1 clear goal)
❌ 'Recruit and sell and train'
✅ 'Recruit 5 new members in 72 hours'

2. TARGET (Who exactly)
❌ 'Everyone'
✅ 'People who engaged with health content in last 30 days'

3. MESSAGE (Core communication)
❌ Multiple messages for multiple goals
✅ ONE message, ONE offer, ONE CTA

4. CHANNELS (Where to reach them)
❌ 'Post on everything'
✅ 'Zalo group + personal DMs + 1 event'

5. TIMELINE (When)
❌ 'Whenever we get around to it'
✅ 'Day 1: 8am launch, Day 2: 2pm webinar, Day 3: 8pm close'

6. BUDGET (What it costs)
❌ 'Spend whatever'
✅ '50K for gifts, 2 hrs/day leader time, 1 event'

7. METRICS (How to measure)
❌ 'Feel successful'
✅ '5 recruits, 20 presentations, 200 reaches'

CAMPAIGN DECISION TREE:

When should you run a campaign?
✅ PSN has stable baseline (systems working)
✅ Team has capacity (not overloaded)
✅ Opportunity exists (market window, product launch)
✅ Resources available (time, budget, energy)

When NOT to campaign:
❌ PSN systems broken (recruits will leave)
❌ Team already burned out
❌ No clear objective
❌ No preparation time

Action items:
1. Audit current PSN: Are systems stable enough for a campaign?
2. Choose 1 campaign type for next month
3. Block calendar time for campaign preparation

lessons.title: Campaign Design Framework — Thiết kế chiến dịch
lessons.objective: Master the complete campaign design process
lessons.content:
Campaign design là science + art. Science = framework và process. Art = messaging và timing.

CAMPAIGN CANVAS (1-page template):

=== CAMPAIGN CANVAS ===

1. CAMPAIGN NAME:
Catchy, memorable, descriptive
VD: 'PSN Health Blitz — Tháng 6/2026'

2. PRIMARY OBJECTIVE:
ONE clear, measurable goal
- Recruitment: '5 new members'
- Sales: '20 orders / 6 triệu revenue'
- Awareness: '500 new connections'
- Retention: 'Re-engage 10 inactive members'

3. SECONDARY OBJECTIVES (Max 2):
- Build content library
- Train team on new skills
- Test new approach

4. TARGET AUDIENCE:
Demographics:
- Age: ___
- Gender: ___
- Location: ___
- Income: ___

Psychographics:
- Health consciousness level: ___
- Tech adoption: ___
- Values: ___

Behaviors:
- Where they spend time online: ___
- What content they engage with: ___
- Purchase triggers: ___

Size estimate: ___ people reachable

5. CORE MESSAGE:
One sentence that captures everything:
'___' (under 15 words)

Supporting messages:
- Message 2 (emotional hook): '___'
- Message 3 (rational proof): '___'
- Message 4 (call to action): '___'

6. CHANNEL MIX:
Primary (70% effort): ___
Secondary (20%): ___
Tertiary (10%): ___

Channel tactics:
- ___: What, when, how many
- ___: What, when, how many

7. TIMELINE:
Preparation: Days ___
Launch: Day ___
Peak: Days ___
Close: Day ___
Follow-up: Days ___

8. BUDGET:
- Content creation: ___K
- Events/gifts: ___K
- Tools/software: ___K
- Contingency (10%): ___K
- Total: ___K

9. TEAM ROLES:
Leader: ___
Content: ___
Connects: ___ members × ___ connects/day
Events: ___
Tracking: ___

10. METRICS:
- Reach target: ___
- Engagement target: ___
- Conversion target: ___
- Revenue target: ___K

11. CONTINGENCIES:
If ___ happens → ___
If ___ happens → ___
=========

CAMPAIGN DESIGN PROCESS (4 steps):

Step 1: OBJECTIVE LOCK (30 min)
- Define primary objective (one sentence)
- Set numbers: exact targets
- Success criteria: What does 'done well' look like?
- Failure threshold: Below what number = this failed?

Step 2: AUDIENCE DEEP DIVE (1 hour)
- Who exactly are we reaching?
- What do they care about?
- Where are they? (channels)
- When are they most receptive?
- What message will resonate?

Step 3: MESSAGE & CHANNEL DESIGN (2 hours)
- Core message: ONE idea, ONE CTA
- Channel strategy: Primary + secondary + tertiary
- Content plan: What to create for each channel
- Timing plan: When to post, when to DM, when to event

Step 4: EXECUTION PLAN (1 hour)
- Timeline: Gantt-style, every day
- Roles: Who does what, by when
- Budget: Every line item
- Metrics: Dashboard setup, tracking template

CAMPAIGN DESIGN PRINCIPLES:

1. FOCUS: One objective, one message, one CTA
2. SIMPLICITY: If you can't explain it in 1 sentence, it's too complex
3. URGENCY: Every campaign needs time-bound element
4. SOCIAL PROOF: Include testimonials, numbers, stories
5. CLEAR CTA: Every piece of content tells them exactly what to do
6. MEASURABILITY: If you can't measure it, don't run it

Action items:
1. Fill out Campaign Canvas for next campaign
2. Define target audience with 3+ specific characteristics
3. Write core message in 15 words or less
4. Create timeline Gantt (even rough)

lessons.title: Flash Campaign — 72-Hour Recruitment Engine
lessons.objective: Design và structure 72-hour recruitment campaign end-to-end
lessons.content:
72-Hour Recruitment Campaign là highest-impact campaign format. Compressed timeline = high urgency = high action rate.

72-HOUR STRUCTURE:

PRE-CAMPAIGN (Days -7 to -1):

7 days before:
- [ ] Identify 50 prospects (warm market list)
- [ ] Prepare 7 days of content (carousel, reels, stories)
- [ ] Write DM scripts (opening, follow-up, closing)
- [ ] Create event/workshop (online Zalo call or offline meetup)
- [ ] Brief team: targets, roles, timeline
- [ ] Prepare tracking sheet

3 days before:
- [ ] Teaser content: 'Something big coming...'
- [ ] Send save-the-date to top 20 prospects
- [ ] Prepare giveaways/prizes cho participants

1 day before:
- [ ] Final team briefing (30 min call)
- [ ] All content scheduled
- [ ] Tracking sheet shared
- [ ] Leader energy = MAX

DAY 1: AWARENESS BLAST (24 giờ)
Goal: Reach 200+ people, generate 50+ expressions of interest

Morning (6:00-8:00):
- Leader: Personal message to top 20 prospects
- Pinned post in PSN group: Campaign announcement
- Energy message to team

Midday (10:00-12:00):
- Content blast: 3 posts (FB, Zalo Moments, Zalo Group)
- Team: 20 connects each, campaign-themed opening
- All DMs mention campaign

Afternoon (14:00-16:00):
- Follow-up on morning connects
- Event registration push (webinar/meetup link)
- Social proof: 'Already 15 people registered!'

Evening (19:00-21:00):
- Live teaser: 30-min Zalo Live about campaign
- Q&A session
- Last call for Day 1 registrations

Day 1 Metrics:
- Reach: ___ (target: 200+)
- Expressions of interest: ___ (target: 50+)
- Event registrations: ___ (target: 30+)
- DMs received: ___

DAY 2: INTEREST BUILDING (24 giờ)
Goal: Deepen interest, host event, get commitments

Morning:
- Reminder messages to registered prospects
- Content: Value posts (not salesy)
- Team connects: 15/day, focus on registered prospects

Midday:
- THE EVENT (2-3 hours):
  - Part 1: Value (30 min) — Health topic, education
  - Part 2: Story (20 min) — Your Droppii journey
  - Part 3: Opportunity (20 min) — Business model reveal
  - Part 4: Q&A (30 min) — Answer objections
  - Part 5: Onboarding (remainder) — Sign up new members

Afternoon:
- Event follow-up to all attendees
- Personal 1:1 with interested prospects
- Send registration link to people who expressed interest but didn't register

Evening:
- Last-chance messaging: 'Event recording available for 24 hours only'
- Personal calls to hot prospects

Day 2 Metrics:
- Event attendance: ___ (target: 25+)
- Presentations given: ___ (target: 15+)
- Decision-stage prospects: ___
- Onboarding started: ___

DAY 3: CONVERSION PUSH (24 giờ)
Goal: Close deals, onboard new members, celebrate

Morning:
- 'Last day' urgency messaging
- Personal follow-ups with decision-stage prospects
- Fast-track onboarding for ready-to-join

Midday:
- Limited-time bonus: 'Join in next 12 hours, get ___.'
- Team blitz: Everyone on connects
- Leader: Personal calls to top 5 prospects

Afternoon:
- Final push: 'This is it — last chance'
- Onboarding support for new members
- Celebration content for PSN group

Evening:
- Campaign close message
- Results announcement
- Celebration of wins
- Thank you to team

Day 3 Metrics:
- New members joined: ___ (target: 5+)
- Orders closed: ___
- Revenue: ___K (target: ___K)
- Conversion rate: ___%

POST-CAMPAIGN (Days +1 to +3):

Day +1:
- Post-mortem analysis
- Celebrate wins trong PSN group
- Follow up with near-misses (interested but didn't join)

Day +2:
- Onboard new members (M1 training)
- Buddy assignments
- Set individual targets for new members

Day +3:
- Team debrief: What worked, what didn't
- Update campaign playbook
- Rest: Leader and team need recovery day

CONVERSION FUNNEL METRICS:

Track each stage:

Awareness → Interest: Target 25% (50/200)
Interest → Registration: Target 60% (30/50)
Registration → Attendance: Target 80% (24/30)
Attendance → Decision: Target 40% (10/24)
Decision → Join: Target 50% (5/10)

Bottleneck analysis:
- If Awareness→Interest low: Content not compelling enough
- If Interest→Registration low: Registration process too hard
- If Registration→Attendance low: No reminder system
- If Attendance→Decision low: Presentation not persuasive
- If Decision→Join low: Onboarding/close not smooth

Action items:
1. Design 72-hour recruitment campaign using framework above
2. Identify 50 prospects for next campaign
3. Prepare 3 content pieces for Day 1
4. Schedule campaign date

lessons.title: Flash Campaign Execution — Day 1: Awareness Blast
lessons.objective: Execute Day 1 of recruitment campaign with maximum reach
lessons.content:
Day 1 = AWARENESS. Goal: Maximum reach, generate interest, get registrations.

DAY 1 EXECUTION PLAYBOOK:

06:00-07:00 | LEADER PERSONAL OUTREACH (Priority)
- Send personal Zalo DMs to top 20 prospects
- Template: 'Hi [Name], đang có event thú vị về sức khỏe thứ 7 này. Mình nghĩ bạn sẽ thích. Mình register cho bạn nhé?'
- Goal: 10+ replies from top 20

07:00-08:00 | MORNING CONTENT BLAST
- Post 1: Zalo Moments — Photo + story about upcoming event
- Post 2: Zalo Group — Announcement với urgency
- Post 3: Facebook — Event page created, invite friends

Content specs:
- Visual: Professional but authentic photo
- Text: Short, punchy, curiosity-driven
- CTA: 'Comment YES để mình gửi link'

08:00-10:00 | TEAM ACTIVATION
- Send team message: 'Campaign Day 1 — let's go!'
- Brief: 20 connects each, use campaign opening line
- Target: 20 members × 20 connects = 400 connects
- Track in shared sheet

10:00-12:00 | FOLLOW-UP BLAST
- Reply to ALL comments from morning posts
- Follow up on morning DMs
- Send event registration link to interested people
- Update tracking: replies → registrations

12:00-14:00 | LUNCH ENGAGEMENT
- Post quick engagement content in group: 'Poll: Sức khỏe là priority của bạn không? A/B/C'
- Respond to all poll participants personally
- Goal: 30+ poll responses, 10+ follow-up conversations

14:00-16:00 | AFTERNOON CONTENT
- Post 2: Educational content (related to campaign theme)
- Post 3: Social proof — 'Thành viên mới tuần này đạt...'
- Team: Continue connects (afternoon batch)

16:00-18:00 | REGISTRATION PUSH
- Target people who engaged but haven't registered
- Messages: 'Bạn đã comment YES — đây là link event. Free participation!'
- Create urgency: 'Chỉ còn 15 slots'

19:00-21:00 | EVENING ENGAGEMENT
- Zalo Live (30 min): Teaser about tomorrow's event
- Share 1 customer story/testimonial
- Final push: 'Last registrations for tomorrow'

21:00-22:00 | DAY 1 REVIEW
- Count: Reach, registrations, DMs, replies
- Compare to targets
- Adjust Day 2 strategy based on Day 1 data

DAY 1 SUCCESS METRICS:

Minimum: 100 reach, 25 registrations
Target: 200 reach, 50 registrations, 20 event signups
Stretch: 400 reach, 80 registrations, 35 event signups

COMMON DAY 1 MISTAKES:

❌ Posting once and waiting: Content needs 3-5 touchpoints/day
❌ Generic messaging: Every DM should be personalized
❌ No tracking: Can't optimize what you don't measure
❌ Leader inactive: Leader must be MOST active on Day 1
❌ Forgetting follow-up: Interest dies within 2 hours — reply fast

Action items:
1. Write 3 Day 1 content pieces (morning, afternoon, evening)
2. Prepare DM templates (top 20 personal, mass follow-up)
3. Set up tracking sheet for all metrics
4. Schedule all posts for Day 1

lessons.title: Flash Campaign Execution — Day 2: Interest & Event
lessons.objective: Execute Day 2: Host event, build interest, get commitments
lessons.content:
Day 2 = INTEREST & DECISION. This is THE day. Event quality determines campaign success.

DAY 2 STRUCTURE:

Morning (8:00-10:00):
- Final reminders to registered attendees
- Personal DMs to warm prospects who haven't registered
- Content: 'Today is the day! Who's coming?'
- Team connects: Focus on getting last-minute registrations

Midday (12:00-14:00): PRE-EVENT PREP
- Test tech: Zalo call link, audio, video
- Prepare materials: slides, product samples, registration form
- Team briefing: Roles during event (greeter, chat monitor, follow-up)
- Leader prep: Presentation flow, key messages, objection responses

14:00-17:00 | THE EVENT (3 hours)

=== EVENT STRUCTURE ===

Part 1: OPENING (15 min) — Welcome + Energy
- Greet everyone, make them feel welcome
- Quick icebreaker: 'Raise tay ai ở HCM / HN / ĐN / Other'
- Set expectations: 'Today có value + surprise'
- Introduce team members

Part 2: VALUE (30 min) — Educational Content
- Health topic: '3 bước Medicine 3.0 cho gia đình Việt'
- Personal story: Why you got into this
- Credibility building: Results, testimonials
- Engagement: Ask questions, poll responses

Part 3: BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY (25 min) — The Reveal
- Transition: 'Và đây là cách tôi build sự nghiệp xung quanh điều này'
- Business model: Simple, visual explanation
- Income potential: Realistic numbers (not hype)
- Why Droppii: Differentiation vs competitors
- Your personal results: Real numbers

Part 4: SOCIAL PROOF (15 min) — Proof it Works
- Customer testimonials (3-5 people)
- Team member success stories
- Before/after transformations
- Live proof: Show app, show orders, show earnings

Part 5: Q&A (30 min) — Handle Objections
- Open floor for questions
- Common objections prepared:
  - 'Có đáng tin không?' → 'Tôi hiểu. Đây là evidence...'
  - 'Tôi không có kinh nghiệm' → 'Chính tôi cũng không, bắt đầu từ zero'
  - 'Cần invest nhiều không?' → 'Bắt đầu với ___K, test trước'
  - 'Thời gian thế nào?' → 'Part-time, 2-3 tiếng/ngày'
  - 'Tôi không giỏi bán hàng' → 'Không cần sell — bạn share value'
- Always close with: 'Ai đã có thêm câu hỏi?' (silence = interest)

Part 6: ONBOARDING (30 min) — For Ready-to-Join
- Registration process walkthrough
- First steps: App download, account setup, first order
- Buddy assignment
- Welcome message
- Next 7-day plan

Part 7: CLOSE (10 min) — Urgency + Next Steps
- Recap: What we covered, what's possible
- Urgency: 'Registration bonus ends tonight at midnight'
- Clear CTA: 'Comment JOIN hoặc inbox mình'
- Gratitude: Thank attendees, celebrate interest
- Next event teaser

=== END EVENT ===

Afternoon (16:00-18:00):
- Event follow-up: Message ALL attendees
- Tier 1: Joined → Onboard immediately
- Tier 2: Interested, needs follow-up → Schedule 1:1
- Tier 3: Not ready → Nurture sequence

Evening (19:00-21:00):
- Personal calls to hot prospects
- Event recording available for 24 hours
- Reminder: 'Last chance for registration bonus'

Event quality checkpoints:
- [ ] Audio/video tested before start
- [ ] Opening energy HIGH
- [ ] Value content substantive (not fluff)
- [ ] Business reveal clear (not confusing)
- [ ] Social proof authentic (real people, real results)
- [ ] Q&A handles top 5 objections
- [ ] Onboarding smooth for new members
- [ ] Close has urgency + clear CTA

Action items:
1. Design event flow (Part 1-7 above)
2. Prepare 3 testimonials for social proof section
3. Write objection response scripts for top 5 objections
4. Prepare onboarding checklist for new members

lessons.title: Flash Campaign Execution — Day 3: Conversion Push
lessons.objective: Execute Day 3: Final push, close deals, celebrate wins
lessons.content:
Day 3 = CONVERSION. Final push. Maximum effort. Close everything that's closable.

DAY 3 STRUCTURE:

Morning (6:00-9:00): LAST CHANCE BLAST

Message 1 (6:00) — PSN Group:
'🔴 LAST DAY! Campaign closes tonight at midnight. Đây là last chance để:
✅ Join PSN với registration bonus
✅ Nhận ưu đãi đặc biệt
✅ Bắt đầu hành trình Droppii
→ Comment JOIN hoặc inbox ngay!'

Message 2 (7:00) — Personal DMs:
To all decision-stage prospects:
'[Name], tôi biết bạn đang consider. Tôi muốn give you one last thing: [specific bonus/incentive]. This expires tonight. Can we talk for 5 min?'

Message 3 (8:00) — Event recording reminder:
'Recording của event hôm qua available đến TONIGHT ONLY. Sau 12h, link die. Watch rồi comment nếu bạn interested.'

Midday (10:00-14:00): CONNECT BLITZ

Every team member:
- 25 connects (higher than usual — campaign mode)
- Campaign-specific DM script:
  Opening: 'Hey [Name], cuối tuần có campaign đặc biệt. Đây là last chance — bạn có interested không?'
  Follow-up: 'Tôi có thể reserve slot cho bạn. What do you think?'
- Track: Connects → Responses → Commitments

Leader actions:
- Personal calls to top 10 prospects (15-20 min each)
- Handle objections in real-time
- Close decisions

Afternoon (14:00-18:00): ONBOARDING MARATHON

For each new member who joins:

Step 1: Welcome (5 min)
- Zalo message: 'Chào mừng đến PSN [name]! Tôi rất vui bạn ở đây.'
- Send welcome pack: M1 overview, app download link

Step 2: Setup (15 min)
- Guide through app registration
- First product order (if applicable)
- Set up habit tracker

Step 3: First targets (10 min)
- Week 1 targets: 5 connects/day, M1 modules
- Buddy assignment
- First meeting invitation

Step 4: Celebration (5 min)
- PSN group announcement: 'Welcome [Name] to the team! 🎉'
- Emoji storm from team
- Personal motivation: 'You made a great decision.'

Evening (19:00-23:00): FINAL PUSH + CLOSE

19:00 — Final reminder blast:
'⏰ 4 HOURS LEFT! Campaign closes at midnight. Đây là last opportunity. Inbox mình NOW nếu bạn không muốn miss out.'

20:00 — Scarcity message:
'Slots đang fill nhanh. Còn 3 spots với registration bonus.'

21:00 — Final event recording push:
'Recording expires in 1 hour. Watch now: [link]'

22:00 — Last call:
'1 HOUR LEFT. Last chance. Inbox NOW.'

23:00 — Final push:
'30 MINUTES. This is truly last call.'

23:30 — LAST FINAL:
'15 MINUTES. Comment LAST if you still want in.'

23:59 — CAMPAIGN CLOSE
- Close all offers
- Thank you message to everyone who engaged

DAY 3 CLOSING (Day +1 morning):

Results announcement trong PSN group:
'🎉 CAMPAIGN RESULTS 🎉
New members: ___ (target: 5+)
Revenue: ___K (target: ___K)
Connects: ___ (team total)
Event attendance: ___

THANK YOU to everyone who participated. Especially:
🏆 Top recruiter: [Name] — ___ recruits
🏆 Top connector: [Name] — ___ connects
🏆 Best energy: [Name] — kept team motivated throughout'

POST-CAMPAIGN SEQUENCE:

For new members (Days +1 to +7):
- Day +1: Welcome + onboarding start
- Day +2: First coaching session
- Day +3: Check-in: 'How's first week?'
- Day +5: First order support
- Day +7: Week 1 review

For prospects who didn't join:
- Day +1: 'Thanks for your interest. No pressure — when you're ready...'
- Day +3: Share valuable content
- Day +7: Soft re-invite: 'We're doing another event next month'
- Day +14: Check in, stay warm
- Day +30: Re-approach with new angle

Action items:
1. Write Day 3 urgency messaging sequence (6 messages)
2. Create new member onboarding checklist
3. Write post-campaign follow-up sequence (for joins and near-misses)
4. Schedule campaign close time and prepare results template

lessons.title: A/B Testing Fundamentals — Khoa học thử nghiệm
lessons.objective: Master A/B testing methodology for campaigns and funnels
lessons.content:
A/B testing = scientific method for marketing. Instead of guessing what works, TEST it.

A/B TEST ANATOMY:

Every test has:

1. HYPOTHESIS
'If I change X, then Y will improve because Z'
❌ Bad: 'Let's test if morning posts work better'
✅ Good: 'If I change post time from 9am to 7am, then response rate will increase by 20% because people check Zalo before work'

2. VARIABLES
- Control (A): Current approach
- Variant (B): New approach
- ONLY ONE difference between A and B

3. SAMPLE SIZE
Minimum: 20-30 per variant for directional insight
Statistical significance: 100+ per variant

4. DURATION
Minimum: 3 days (capture weekly patterns)
Ideal: 7 days (full week cycle)
Maximum: 14 days (beyond this, external factors contaminate)

5. SUCCESS METRIC
Primary: ONE main metric (response rate, conversion rate, etc.)
Secondary: Supporting metrics

6. DECISION RULE
Pre-defined: 'If B beats A by X%, we adopt B'

A/B TEST DESIGN CHECKLIST:

Before running test:
- [ ] Hypothesis clearly stated
- [ ] Only ONE variable changed
- [ ] Sample size calculated
- [ ] Duration set
- [ ] Success metric defined
- [ ] Decision rule pre-defined
- [ ] Tracking system ready

STATISTICAL SIGNIFICANCE:

You need enough data to know the result is real, not random.

Quick guide:
- 20-30 samples per variant: Directional (use for guidance)
- 50-100 per variant: Reasonable confidence
- 100+ per variant: High confidence
- 500+ per variant: Very high confidence

Rule of thumb: If difference > 20%, you can trust it with 50+ samples.
If difference 5-20%, need 100+ samples.
If difference < 5%, need 500+.

WHAT TO TEST (Priority Order):

HIGH IMPACT (Test these first):
1. Opening lines in DMs (massive impact on response rate)
2. Post timing (morning vs evening, day of week)
3. Offer/Promotion (what you're offering, how you frame it)
4. Target audience (who you're reaching)

MEDIUM IMPACT:
5. Message format (text, image, video, carousel)
6. Content length (short vs long)
7. CTA wording ('Comment YES' vs 'Inbox me' vs 'Click link')
8. Follow-up timing (1 hour vs 3 hours vs next day)

LOW IMPACT:
9. Emoji usage
10. Greeting style (formal vs casual)
11. Signature/name format

COMMON A/B TEST MISTAKES:

❌ Testing too many variables at once
'Let's test morning posts with images and different copy' = testing 3 variables
→ Fix: Change ONE thing per test

❌ Stopping test too early
'After 1 day, B is winning — let's switch!'
→ Fix: Run full duration. Early results are often random.

❌ No statistical significance
'2 out of 3 people preferred B'
→ Fix: Need minimum sample size before deciding

❌ Cherry-picking data
'Let's look at the 2 days where B won'
→ Fix: Look at ALL data from full test period

❌ Testing inconsequential things
'Does blue button convert better than green?''
→ Fix: Test things that could move the needle 20%+

❌ Never implementing the winner
'Test was interesting but we kept doing what we always did'
→ Fix: When test is conclusive, IMPLEMENT the winner immediately

A/B TEST SCHEDULE:

Week 1: Test connect timing (morning vs evening)
Week 2: Test DM opening lines (question vs statement)
Week 3: Test content format (image vs carousel vs video)
Week 4: Test CTA wording
Week 5-8: Test offers, target segments, follow-up sequences

Action items:
1. Write hypothesis for your first A/B test
2. Calculate required sample size
3. Set up tracking system
4. Run first test this week

lessons.title: A/B Test Design — Recruitment Funnel Deep Dive
lessons.objective: Design comprehensive A/B tests for recruitment funnel stages
lessons.content:
Recruitment funnel có 5 stages. Mỗi stage có variables khác nhau để test.

RECRUITMENT FUNNEL STAGES:

1. AWARENESS (They know you exist)
2. INTEREST (They want to know more)
3. CONSIDERATION (They're evaluating)
4. DECISION (They want to join)
5. ONBOARDING (They're now a member)

A/B TESTS PER STAGE:

=== STAGE 1: AWARENESS → INTEREST ===

Test variables:

A. Content type:
- A: Educational post (health tip)
- B: Story post (personal journey)
- C: Opportunity post (business invite)
- Measure: Engagement rate (reactions + comments + shares)

B. Content format:
- A: Single image
- B: Carousel (3-5 slides)
- C: Video/reel
- Measure: Reach + engagement rate

C. Post timing:
- A: 6:00-8:00 (morning)
- B: 12:00-14:00 (lunch)
- C: 20:00-22:00 (evening)
- Measure: Engagement rate + reach

D. Post frequency:
- A: 1 post/day
- B: 3 posts/day
- Measure: Engagement per post + follower growth

=== STAGE 2: INTEREST → CONSIDERATION ===

Test variables:

A. DM opening line:
- A: 'Chào bạn, bạn có khỏe không?'
- B: 'Mình thấy bạn quan tâm về sức khỏe. Mình có điều thú vị muốn share.'
- C: 'Hey! Quick question — bạn đang tìm cách improve health không?'
- Measure: Response rate

B. Follow-up timing:
- A: Immediate (within 1 hour)
- B: Same day (4-6 hours later)
- C: Next day
- Measure: Response rate + conversation quality

C. Message length:
- A: Short (1-2 sentences)
- B: Medium (3-4 sentences)
- C: Long (paragraph)
- Measure: Response rate

=== STAGE 3: CONSIDERATION → DECISION ===

Test variables:

A. Presentation format:
- A: 1:1 personal meeting (coffee)
- B: Group webinar (Zalo call)
- C: Video presentation + Q&A
- Measure: Decision rate

B. Social proof type:
- A: Numbers ('500+ customers, 50+ leaders')
- B: Stories ('Đây là hành trình của An...')
- C: Testimonials ('Đây là feedback của Khánh...')
- Measure: Trust/engagement during presentation

C. Offer structure:
- A: Product only (experience first)
- B: Business opportunity (join first, product later)
- C: Both (experience + opportunity in one)
- Measure: Conversion rate

=== STAGE 4: DECISION → ONBOARDING ===

Test variables:

A. Onboarding speed:
- A: Same-day onboarding (within 2 hours of join)
- B: Next-day onboarding
- C: Scheduled onboarding (their choice)
- Measure: First order rate + Day 7 retention

B. First experience:
- A: Product experience (order, try, feel)
- B: Training experience (modules, learning)
- C: Community experience (PSN meeting, meet team)
- Measure: Engagement score after Day 7

C. Buddy assignment:
- A: Immediate buddy assignment
- B: Buddy after Day 3
- C: Self-selected buddy
- Measure: Day 14 retention

SEQUENTIAL TESTING STRATEGY:

Don't test everything at once. Sequence:

Month 1: Fix biggest bottleneck
- Identify: Which stage has lowest conversion?
- Test: Variables at that stage
- Goal: Improve that stage by 20%+

Month 2: Optimize next bottleneck
- Move to next lowest conversion stage
- Test relevant variables

Month 3: Full funnel optimization
- Test interactions between stages
- Holistic optimization

Example sequence:
Month 1: Awareness → Interest (test content type, timing)
Month 2: Interest → Consideration (test DM opening, follow-up)
Month 3: Consideration → Decision (test presentation format)
Month 4: Decision → Onboarding (test onboarding experience)

FUNNEL OPTIMIZATION PRINCIPLES:

1. SMALL IMPROVEMENTS COMPOUND:
- Each stage +5% = overall funnel +27% (compounding effect)
- 5 stages × +5% each = massive total improvement

2. FIX LEAKIEST BUCKET FIRST:
- 50% drop at Stage 2 = fix Stage 2 before optimizing Stage 1
- Biggest ROI from fixing worst stage

3. TEST ONE STAGE AT A TIME:
- Don't change Stage 1 AND Stage 2 simultaneously
- Isolate variables to know what worked

4. MEASURE FUNNEL-WIDE:
- Improving one stage might hurt another
- Always look at overall funnel, not just one stage

Action items:
1. Map your current recruitment funnel with actual conversion rates
2. Identify lowest-converting stage
3. Design A/B test for that stage (2 variants, clear hypothesis)
4. Set up tracking and run test for 7 days

lessons.title: A/B Test Execution — Chạy thử nghiệm
lessons.objective: Execute A/B tests properly: setup, run, collect data without bias
lessons.content:
Execution phase: Where plans become data. Precision matters.

A/B TEST EXECUTION PROTOCOL:

PRE-TEST (Day 0):

Setup:
- [ ] Create tracking spreadsheet with columns:
  Date | Variant | Reach | Engagement | Response | Conversion | Notes
- [ ] Define audience split (random, 50/50)
- [ ] Prepare all content/scripts for both variants
- [ ] Brief team (if applicable): Which variant, how to track
- [ ] Set calendar reminders for check-ins

Randomization:
- Use Zalo contact list, split alphabetically (A-M = Variant A, N-Z = Variant B)
- Or alternate: 1st contact = A, 2nd = B, 3rd = A...
- DO NOT cherry-pick: 'These look like A material'

TEST RUN (Days 1-7):

Daily routine:

Morning:
- Execute variant assignments
- Record data in tracking sheet
- Note any anomalies or observations

Evening:
- Quick check: Are both variants getting equal volume?
- Any unexpected patterns?
- Note observations for analysis

Monitoring checkpoints:

Day 2: Equal volume check
- Variant A: ___ connects
- Variant B: ___ connects
- If imbalance > 30%: Adjust next day's assignment

Day 4: Early signal check
- Preliminary response rates
- Directional: Is one variant clearly winning?
- DON'T stop test yet — wait for full data

Day 7: Full data collection
- All data recorded
- Check: Equal-ish sample sizes?
- Proceed to analysis

BIAS PREVENTION:

Common biases to avoid:

1. SELECTION BIAS:
'Let me use the better prospects for variant B'
→ Fix: Random assignment, no cherry-picking

2. CONFIRMATION BIAS:
'I knew A would win' — only noticing data that confirms belief
→ Fix: Pre-commit to decision rule before seeing results

3. RECENCY BIAS:
'Yesterday B won so B is better'
→ Fix: Look at full 7-day dataset

4. SURVIVORSHIP BIAS:
'Everyone who responded liked B'
→ Fix: Also analyze non-responses

lessons.title: A/B Test Analysis — Phân tích và ra quyết định
lessons.objective: Analyze A/B test results statistically and make data-driven decisions
lessons.content:
Analysis = where data becomes wisdom. Raw numbers tell story. Your job: read the story.

A/B TEST ANALYSIS FRAMEWORK:

Step 1: DATA VERIFICATION (10 min)

Before any analysis:
- [ ] All data collected for full test period
- [ ] No missing days
- [ ] Sample sizes roughly equal (within 30%)
- [ ] No external events during test (product launch, holiday, etc.)
- [ ] Both variants executed correctly (no mistakes in execution)

Step 2: DESCRIPTIVE STATS (15 min)

Calculate for each variant:

A Variant:
- Total reach: ___
- Total responses: ___
- Response rate: ___% = (responses / reach) × 100
- Total conversions: ___ (if applicable)
- Conversion rate: ___% = (conversions / responses) × 100

B Variant:
- Same calculations

Comparison table:
| Metric | Variant A | Variant B | Difference |
|--------|-----------|-----------|------------|
| Response rate | ___% | ___% | +/-___% |
| Conv. rate | ___% | ___% | +/-___% |
| Engagement | ___% | ___% | +/-___% |

Step 3: SIGNIFICANCE CHECK (10 min)

Is the difference real or random?

Quick significance guide:
- Difference > 30%: Significant even with 20 samples
- Difference 10-30%: Significant with 50+ samples
- Difference 5-10%: Significant with 100+ samples
- Difference < 5%: Inconclusive, need 500+ samples

Formula intuition:
Larger sample + bigger difference = more confident
Smaller sample + smaller difference = probably random

Step 4: SEGMENT ANALYSIS (15 min)

Don't just look at totals. Break down by:

- Time of day: Does variant work better at certain times?
- Day of week: Better on Mon vs Fri?
- Prospect type: New contacts vs warm prospects?
- Message personalization: Personalized vs generic?

Hidden insights often live in segments.
Example: Overall A and B similar, BUT A works 2x better on warm prospects while B works 2x better on cold prospects.

Step 5: QUALITATIVE ANALYSIS (15 min)

Numbers don't tell the whole story. Look at:

Response quality:
- Variant A responses: Short 'Ok' vs Variant B responses: Detailed questions
- Quality > quantity sometimes

Conversation flow:
- Which variant led to longer conversations?
- Which led to faster decision-making?
- Which generated more objections?

Unexpected patterns:
- Did one variant work on days the other didn't?
- Did team member execution quality affect results?
- Were there any surprises?

Step 6: DECISION (10 min)

Four possible outcomes:

OUTCOME 1: CLEAR WINNER
- B beats A by 20%+ with sufficient sample
→ Decision: Implement B as new standard
→ Timeline: This week

OUTCOME 2: TIE
- Results within 5% of each other
→ Decision: Keep A (no need to change what works)
→ Or choose based on secondary metrics (easier to execute, team preference)

OUTCOME 3: INCONCLUSIVE
- Small sample, marginal difference
→ Decision: Run larger test with 2x sample size
→ Or test different variable if this one seems unimportant

OUTCOME 4: SURPRISE WINNER
- C variant (neither A nor B) actually performed best
→ Decision: Design new test based on surprise insight
→ 'The opening line nobody tested actually worked best — why?'

Step 7: DOCUMENT & SCALE (10 min)

- Document results in playbook
- If winner found: Update standard operating procedure
- If insight found: Add to knowledge base
- Share with team: 'Here's what we learned'
- Schedule next test

ANALYSIS PITFALLS:

❌ P-hacking: Looking at data until something looks significant
→ Fix: Pre-define success metric and threshold

❌ Ignoring confidence intervals
→ Fix: Always note sample size when reporting results

❌ Over-interpreting small samples
→ Fix: Under 50 samples = directional only, not conclusive

❌ Changing test mid-run
→ Fix: Run full duration, even if one variant seems to be winning early

❌ Multiple testing without correction
→ Fix: If running 10 tests, expect 1 false positive by chance

Action items:
1. Complete statistical analysis of your A/B test
2. Calculate significance level
3. Make decision: adopt winner / retest / new hypothesis
4. Document results in campaign playbook

lessons.title: Flash Campaign 2 — Sales Push Execution
lessons.objective: Design và execute 48-hour flash sales campaign
lessons.content:
Campaign 2 = SALES PUSH. 48-hour flash sale. Different from recruitment: shorter, more urgent, product-focused.

SALES CAMPAIGN DESIGN:

CAMPAIGN OFFER STRUCTURE:

Great flash sale offer has 4 elements:

1. PRODUCT BUNDLE
- Combine 2-3 products into one package
- Price: Bundle giá < sum of individual prices
- Example: 'Wellness Starter Pack — 3 sản phẩm chỉ 990K (giá gốc 1.4M)'

2. LIMITED QUANTITY
- 'Chỉ 50 packages available'
- Creates FOMO (fear of missing out)
- Real limit: Actually limit it

3. LIMITED TIME
- '48 hours only — từ 20/6 00:00 đến 22/6 23:59'
- Clear deadline, unambiguous

4. BONUS VALUE
- 'Mua trong 24h đầu, tặng thêm: E-book + Coaching session'
- Increases perceived value
- Time-bound bonus adds urgency

48-HOUR TIMELINE:

- [ ] Build anticipation trong PSN group
- [ ] Personal messages to likely buyers: 'You might want this...'
- [ ] Prepare all materials: product photos, bundle details, order form

  Pinned post: '🔥 FLASH SALE — 48 HOURS ONLY 🔥'

  Personal DMs to top 30 prospects

HOUR 12-24 (Launch Day Afternoon + Evening):

- Urgency content: '40 packages remaining'
- Q&A content: Answer top 3 questions about products
- Team continues sharing

HOUR 24-36 (Day 2 Morning + Afternoon):

- 'Only 25 packages remaining'
- Last-chance messaging
- Personal calls to hot prospects

HOUR 36-48 (Day 2 Evening):

HOUR 47-48 (Final 2 Hours):

- Leader: Personal DM to everyone who engaged but didn't order

HOUR 48: CLOSE

'So với uống cafe mỗi ngày: 33K/ngày'

ORDER TRACKING:

lessons.title: Multi-Channel Campaign Design — Triệt để đa kênh
lessons.objective: Design integrated campaigns across multiple channels for maximum reach
lessons.content:
Multi-channel campaign = nhắm đến audience qua nhiều touchpoints. Each channel có strengths. Combined = compound effect.

CHANNEL STRENGTHS:

ZALO:
- Strength: Direct, personal, high response rate
- Best for: DM campaigns, group engagement, personal outreach
- Content: Text + image, short video
- Frequency: Multiple per day ok (personal DMs limit: 10-15/day)

FACEBOOK:
- Strength: Broad reach, groups, events
- Best for: Public content, community building, event pages
- Content: Posts, stories, reels, live
- Frequency: 1-3 posts/day

INSTAGRAM/TIKTOK:
- Strength: Visual, young audience, viral potential
- Best for: Product demos, lifestyle content, influencer-style
- Content: Reels, carousels, stories
- Frequency: 3-5 posts/week

OFFLINE EVENTS:
- Strength: Deep connection, trust building
- Best for: Closing decisions, team building, product experience
- Format: Coffee meetups, workshop, home party
- Frequency: 1-2/month

ZALO OA (Official Account):
- Strength: Broadcast to many, professional
- Best for: Announcements, customer service, follow-up sequences
- Content: Updates, reminders, offers
- Frequency: 2-3 messages/week (don't spam)

MULTI-CHANNEL CAMPAIGN DESIGN:

Step 1: MESSAGE CONSISTENCY
Core message must be SAME across all channels:
- 'Tháng này chúng tôi giúp 10 gia đình có sức khỏe tốt hơn'
- Same on Zalo, FB, Instagram, event

But EXECUTION differs per channel:
- Zalo: Personal DM to each prospect
- FB: Post + group share
- Instagram: Visual carousel
- Event: Live presentation

Step 2: CHANNEL SEQUENCE

Touchpoint sequence for campaign:

Touch 1 (Day -7): Zalo Moments — Teaser content
Touch 2 (Day -5): Facebook — Event page / announcement
Touch 3 (Day -3): Zalo DM — Personal invitation to top prospects
Touch 4 (Day -1): Zalo Group — Reminder + social proof
Touch 5 (Day 0): EVENT — Live experience
Touch 6 (Day +1): Zalo DM — Follow-up với tất cả attendees
Touch 7 (Day +3): FB — Thank you + next event teaser
Touch 8 (Day +7): Zalo OA — Special offer for responders

Each touch reinforces the same message through different channel.

Step 3: CHANNEL-SPECIFIC CONTENT

Zalo:
- Short, personal, conversational
- 'Hey [Name], sáng nay tôi có content hay về sức khỏe. Check nhé!'
- Response expected: High

Facebook:
- More formal, public-facing
- '3 bước Medicine 3.0 cho người bận rộn — link trong comments'
- Response expected: Medium

Instagram:
- Visual-first, lifestyle-oriented
- Carousel: 'Sức khỏe của bạn U30 — 5 things nobody tells you'
- Response expected: Medium

Events:
- Deep, personal, persuasive
- Live demonstration, Q&A, on-the-spot offers
- Response expected: Very high

CROSS-CHANNEL ORCHESTRATION:

Principle: Each channel supports the others.

Example orchestration for recruitment:

Week 1:
- Zalo: Daily health content (build authority)
- FB: Event page created, invite friends
- Instagram: Behind-the-scenes content
- Zalo DM: Personal invites to top 20 prospects

Week 2:
- Zalo: Event reminders daily
- FB: Event hype content
- Event: The main conversion event
- DM: Last-minute personal invites

Week 3:
- Zalo: Follow-up với attendees
- FB: Thank you + testimonials
- Instagram: Success story content
- Zalo OA: Onboarding sequence for new members

ATTRIBUTION (Track which channel works):

For each new member/customer:
- First touch: Which channel?
- Conversion touch: Which channel?
- Most influential: Which channel?

Track in CRM/spreadsheet:
| Member | Zalo | FB | IG | Event | OA | Primary |
|--------|------|-----|-----|-------|-----|---------|
| [Name] | ✓ | | | ✓ | | Event |

Over time, you'll know: 'Events convert 3x better than DMs for my audience.'

2. Design 1 multi-channel campaign (use sequence above)
3. Create channel-specific content for your next campaign
4. Set up attribution tracking

lessons.title: Campaign Budget & ROI — Tính toán hiệu quả
lessons.objective: Calculate campaign budgets and measure ROI for continuous improvement
lessons.content:
Every campaign has a cost. Every campaign should generate return. Know the numbers.

CAMPAIGN COST BREAKDOWN:

1. DIRECT COSTS:
- Content creation: ___K (designer, photographer, editor)
- Event costs: ___K (venue, food, gifts, materials)
- Advertising: ___K (FB ads, Zalo ads, boosting)
- Gifts/incentives: ___K (products, vouchers, bonuses)
- Tools: ___K (scheduling software, tracking, design tools)

2. INDIRECT COSTS (Often forgotten):
- Leader time: ___ hrs × ___K/hr = ___K
- Team time: ___ members × ___ hrs × ___K/hr = ___K
- Opportunity cost: What else could you have done with this time?

3. TOTAL CAMPAIGN COST: ___K

REVENUE ATTRIBUTION:

Direct revenue from campaign:
- New orders: ___ orders × ___K AOV = ___K
- New members first orders: ___ × ___K = ___K
- Reactivated members: ___ × ___K = ___K
- Total direct: ___K

Indirect revenue (harder to measure):
- New members' future orders (LTV estimate): ___ members × ___K LTV = ___K
- Reactivated members' future orders: ___ × ___K = ___K
- Brand awareness value: Hard to quantify, estimate ___K

ROI CALCULATION:

Direct ROI = (Direct Revenue - Total Cost) / Total Cost × 100%
Example: (500K - 200K) / 200K = 150% ROI

Full ROI (including LTV) = (Direct + Indirect Revenue - Cost) / Cost × 100%
Example: (500K + 800K - 200K) / 200K = 550% ROI

CAMPAIGN ECONOMICS:

Key ratios to track:

Cost per Acquisition (CPA):
CPA = Total Cost / New Customers
Target: < 30% of AOV
Example: AOV = 300K, CPA target = <90K

Customer Lifetime Value (LTV):
LTV = Average monthly spend × Average retention (months)
Example: 150K/month × 12 months = 1.8M LTV

LTV:CPA Ratio:
Target: > 3:1 (LTV 3x higher than CPA)
Example: LTV 1.8M / CPA 90K = 20:1 ✅ Excellent

Payback Period:
Months to recover acquisition cost
= CPA / (AOV × Order frequency)
Example: 90K / (300K × 2/month) = 0.15 months ≈ 5 days

CAMPAIGN BUDGET OPTIMIZATION:

If ROI is low, diagnose:

Low conversion + High CPA:
- Problem: Targeting wrong audience or weak offer
- Fix: Refine targeting, improve offer

High conversion + Low volume:
- Problem: Reaching too few people
- Fix: Increase reach, add channels, boost content

High volume + Low AOV:
- Problem: Attracting bargain hunters
- Fix: Position premium, add value tier

Good numbers + No repeat business:
- Problem: Product experience or follow-up
- Fix: Improve product, add retention campaign

BUDGET ALLOCATION STRATEGY:

For optimal ROI:
- 40% on proven channels (highest ROI historically)
- 30% on testing new channels/tactics
- 20% on brand building (long-term investment)
- 10% contingency

CAMPAIGN SCORECARD:
| Dimension | Score (1-5) |
|-----------|-------------|
| Objective clarity | ___ |
| Target accuracy | ___ |
| Execution quality | ___ |
| Conversion rate | ___ |
| ROI | ___ |
| Team performance | ___ |
| Learning extracted | ___ |
| Overall | ___/35 |

28-35: Exceptional campaign
20-27: Good campaign, some areas to improve
<20: Rethink approach before next campaign

Action items:
1. Calculate true cost of your last campaign (include time)
2. Calculate ROI including LTV estimate
3. Identify budget allocation for next quarter
4. Set CPA target based on AOV

lessons.title: Campaign Automation — Tự động hóa quy trình
lessons.objective: Automate campaign processes to scale without proportional effort increase
lessons.content:
Automation = do more with same effort. Campaign automation focuses on repetitive tasks that don't need human touch.

AUTOMATION OPPORTUNITIES:

Map your campaign process and identify automatable steps:

PRE-CAMPAIGN:
- Content scheduling: Buffer/CapCut scheduler → Auto-post
- Prospect list building: Export from Zalo → Filter → Import
- Brief distribution: Template message → Send to team

CAMPAIGN EXECUTION:
- Social posts: Schedule 7 days in advance
- DM follow-up sequences: Zalo OA auto-reply
- Event reminders: Scheduled messages at T-3, T-1, T+0
- Tracking alerts: Google Sheet → notification when threshold hit

POST-CAMPAIGN:
- Thank you messages: Template → send to all participants
- Follow-up sequences: 3-message sequence over 7 days
- Data aggregation: Auto-pull from sources → summary report
- Next campaign planning: Template-driven calendar

ZALO OA AUTOMATION:

Zalo Official Account = your automation hub:

WELCOME SEQUENCE (New member joins):
- Message 1 (immediate): 'Welcome! Here's what to do first...'
- Message 2 (Day 1): 'Complete your profile and first order'
- Message 3 (Day 3): 'How's it going? Any questions?'
- Message 4 (Day 7): 'Week 1 complete! Here's what's next...'

NURTURE SEQUENCE (Prospect interested, not ready):
- Message 1 (Day 0): 'Thanks for your interest! Here's more info...'
- Message 2 (Day 3): 'Customer story that might resonate...'
- Message 3 (Day 7): 'Quick question — what's holding you back?'
- Message 4 (Day 14): 'We have event coming up. Save the date.'
- Message 5 (Day 30): 'Re-engagement: What would make this right for you?'

RE-ENGAGEMENT SEQUENCE (Dormant member):
- Message 1: 'We miss you! Here's what's new...'
- Message 2 (Day 3): 'Special offer for returning members'
- Message 3 (Day 7): 'PSN misses you — when can we reconnect?'
- Message 4 (Day 14): 'Final check-in — everything okay?'

SOCIAL MEDIA SCHEDULING:

Tools: Buffer, Meta Business Suite, CapCut Scheduler

Weekly scheduling routine (Sunday 30 min):
- Schedule 7 days of posts across platforms
- Mix: 40% educational, 30% personal, 20% opportunity, 10% sales
- Different times: morning, lunch, evening
- Include: images, videos, carousels, stories

ALERT & MONITORING SYSTEMS:

Automated alerts:
- Low habit score alert: When member's score drops below 40
- No order alert: When member has 0 orders for 14 days
- Campaign milestone alert: When campaign reaches 50%/75%/100%
- High engagement alert: When post gets 100+ reactions
- Prospect reply alert: When prospect replies to DM

Alert delivery: Zalo group notification, email, or SMS

CAMPAIGN AUTOMATION CHECKLIST:

Before campaign:
- [ ] Welcome sequence created
- [ ] Nurture sequence created
- [ ] Social posts scheduled
- [ ] Event reminders scheduled
- [ ] Tracking dashboard set up
- [ ] Alert thresholds configured

During campaign:
- [ ] Daily metrics auto-collected
- [ ] Social posts publishing automatically
- [ ] Follow-up messages sending automatically
- [ ] Alerts firing on thresholds
- [ ] Leader focuses on: high-value interactions only

After campaign:
- [ ] Thank you sequence auto-sent
- [ ] Follow-up nurture auto-started
- [ ] Data auto-aggregated into report
- [ ] Next campaign auto-scheduled in calendar

AUTOMATION RULES:

1. Automate REPETITIVE tasks, not RELATIONSHIP tasks
- ✅ Auto-send welcome message
- ❌ Auto-send 'thinking of you' (should be personal)

2. Always have human override
- Automation failsafe: Leader can pause/edit any automated message
- Personal touch for VIP prospects: Never auto-DM top 10 prospects

3. Test automation before going live
- Send test messages to yourself
- Verify timing, content, triggers
- Fix errors before real deployment

4. Keep it simple
- Don't automate everything at once
- Start with 1 sequence, master it, add more
- Simple > Complex

Action items:

2. Set up social media scheduling for next 7 days
3. Configure 3 alert thresholds in your tracking system
4. Document automation workflow

lessons.title: Flash Campaign 3 — Retention & Reactivation
lessons.objective: Execute retention campaign to re-engage inactive members
lessons.content:
Campaign 3 = RETENTION. Getting existing members active again. 5x cheaper than recruiting new ones.

WHY MEMBERS GO DORMANT:

Understanding WHY helps you fix it:

1. ONBOARDING FAILURE
- First experience was confusing
- Didn't understand how to succeed
- No clear first steps
→ Fix: Improve onboarding (M1-M4)

2. LACK OF RESULTS
- No orders after 2-3 weeks
- No recruits, no progress
- 'This isn't working for me'
→ Fix: Early win programs, small achievable targets

3. LOST MOTIVATION
- Original 'why' faded
- No one checking in on them
- Energy of initial excitement gone
→ Fix: Regular motivation, reconnect to WHY

4. EXTERNAL FACTORS
- Busy at work/school
- Family issues
- Health problems
- Financial constraints
→ Fix: Empathy, flexibility, temporary adjustments

5. BETTER ALTERNATIVE
- Found another opportunity
- Competitor recruited them
- Friend invited them elsewhere
→ Fix: Strengthen relationships, increase value

RETENTION CAMPAIGN STRUCTURE (14 ngày):

WEEK 1: REACH (Days 1-7)

Identify dormant members:
- Definition: No connect for 7+ days OR no order for 21+ days
- List: Pull from dashboard
- Segment by: Dormant 7-14 days / 15-30 days / 30+ days

Day 1-2: TIER 1 REACH (Dormant 7-14 days)
- Personal Zalo: 'Hey [Name], haven't seen you in a bit. Everything okay?'
- NOT: 'You haven't been active' (accusatory)
- YES: 'I miss having you around. How are you doing?'
- Response target: 60%+

Day 3-4: TIER 2 REACH (Dormant 15-30 days)
- Personal call (5-10 min Zalo call)
- 'I noticed you've been quiet. Is there something I can help with?'
- Listen to their situation
- Offer specific support: 'Would a 15-min coaching call help?'
- Response target: 40%+

Day 5-7: TIER 3 REACH (Dormant 30+ days)
- Personal message with VALUE
- 'I was thinking about you. Found this article I think you'd love: [link]'
- No ask, just give
- If no response after 2 messages: Mark 'cold', contact in 30 days
- Response target: 20%+

WEEK 2: RE-ENGAGE (Days 8-14)

For members who responded positively:

Day 8: PERSONAL RE-ONBOARDING
- 'Welcome back! Let's get you back on track.'
- Review where they left off
- Set easy first target: 'Today: just log into app'
- Assign/reactivate buddy

Day 9-10: LOW-PRESSURE REINTRODUCTION
- Invite to PSN meeting (as observer, no pressure to participate)
- Share recent PSN wins: 'We had great month!'
- 'No pressure to do anything — just be here'

Day 11-12: GRADUAL REACTIVATION
- Small targets: 3 connects/day (down from 10)
- Easy first order: Small product, fast delivery
- Quick win designed to rebuild confidence

Day 13-14: FULL REINTEGRATION
- Back to normal targets
- Re-assign buddy
- Celebrate return: 'Great to have you back!'
- Track: Day 14 engagement vs baseline

| Tier 2 response rate | 40%+ | ___% |
| Tier 3 response rate | 20%+ | ___% |
| Total reactivated | ___ | ___ |

DORMANT MEMBER BEST PRACTICES:

1. PERSONAL > BLAST
Never send mass 'we miss you' messages. Personal only.

2. VALUE FIRST
Give before asking. Share article, tip, or resource BEFORE inviting them back.

3. NO PRESSURE
'No pressure to do anything' reduces defensiveness.
Pressure = resistance.

4. LISTEN
They left for a reason. Hear it. Don't argue. Don't fix immediately.

5. FLEXIBLE REINTEGRATION
Don't throw them back into 10 connects/day.
Start with 3. Build up. Success breeds success.

6. CELEBRATE RETURN
'So glad you're back!' not 'Where have you been?'
